items.title: Fireworks and tear gas as protesters and riot police clash in Paris
items.summary: Police have clashed with protesters in Paris as some demonstrations in France turned violent on Saturday A largely peaceful day of protests turned into unrest after nightfall, as protesters were seen throwing objects and fireworks at police Around 70,000 officers were deployed across France for a second consecutive weekend and used tear gas and water cannons to disperse crowds The Interior Ministry estimated around 400,000 people took part in Saturday's demonstrations, with nearly 1,000 arrests made Europe correspondent Nick Beake reports from Paris, where he says there are few signs the unrest will ease soon

items.title: Palestinian families displaced as Israeli forces demolish Hebron homes
items.summary: More than 200 families have been displaced, Palestinian officials say The Israeli military has launched a sweeping crackdown in the occupied West Bank, demolishing homes and businesses in the city of Hebron and displacing hundreds of families, according to local officials Footage shared online showed destruction caused by Israeli bulldozers, with at least one whole street appearing to have been flattened. The military has also cordoned off the city, heavily restricting the movement of its 200,000 residents The operation was announced by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday, in response to the killing of two Israeli soldiers by two Palestinian gunmen in an attack on a checkpoint.

items.title: Mozambique: Govt plans 5,541 new civil service hires in 2027, with a budget impact of 1.399 billion meticais
items.summary: According to data from the Economic and Social Plan and State Budget (Plano Económico e Social e Orçamento do Estado – PESOE) compiled today by Lusa, the number of new recruits projected for 2027 represents an increase of 39.9% compared with the 3,962 admissions projected for 2026, while the corresponding budget impact rises by 23.3%, from 1.135 billion meticais (€15.9 million) budgeted for this year to 1.399 billion meticais (€19.6 million) in 2027 Education will continue to account for the largest share of recruitment, with 2,978 admissions planned, equivalent to 53.7% of the total, mainly involving general education teachers. In this sector, the estimated budget impact amounts to 903 million meticais (€12.6 million), corresponding to around two-thirds of the total cost of new admissions planned for next year The proposal also provides for the recruitment of 1,364 employees for the Justice Administration bodies, more than double the 745 admissions planned for 2026.

items.title: Academia urged to present solutions for development challenges
items.summary: Maputo, 23 Oct (AIM) – The Minister of Agriculture, Roberto Mito, has challenged Eduardo Mondlane University (UEM), Mozambique’s oldest higher education institution, to produce scientific guidance that will enable the construction of a resilient economy capable of bringing solutions to the country’s development challenges. Speaking on Thursday at the “First Symposium on Climate Adaptation and Resilience in Mozambique”, held in Maputo, the minister said that the challenge is for the entire Mozambican academic community and if “measures are implemented, they would help the nation reduce its reliance on external funding.” “Science should play a central role in identifying alternatives for national development, helping the country to leverage its existing resources and transform them into a means of financing its own priorities. Mozambique needs to rethink how it mobilizes resources for development and external funding should not come at the expense of the nation’s own capacity to find answers to its challenges.We must find local solutions to address local problems”, he said.

items.title: Muchanga expelled from Renamo for demanding Momade’s resignation
items.summary: Maputo, 23 Oct (AIM) – Renamo party, which used to be Mozambique’s main opposition movement, has decided to expel its best known former parliamentary deputies, António Muchanga, following his suspension last February. Muchanga was one of Renamo’s main speakers in the previous parliament (2019-2024). He continues to speak regularly in television talk shows. Together with demobilized guerrillas, Muchanga has been demanding the resignation of Ossufo Momade from his post as Renamo president. For many months Momade’s opponents have been occupying Renamo offices across the country, demanding his resignation, widely blamed for Renamo’s poor showing in the October 2024 general elections. The former guerrillas also claim that they are being persecuted and even murdered by the current Renamo leadership for demanding Momade’s resignation.
